title: Bug Record v1
description: One record per bug, appended once — no event stream, no fold (v0.5.0 FR2, D11, AR-1). Each line of specs/bugs/BUGS.jsonl is one object validating this schema, keyed by `id`. Every property carries a custom `x-mutability` keyword — `immutable-core` (never rewritten through the record-store update seam once appended), `write-once` (legitimately absent from a freshly registered record; settable exactly once from absent, then immutable), or `mutable-governance` (rewritten in place through the atomic in-place update seam, `core/atomic_write.py` + refuse-stale) — THIS is the one place the three-category split is documented; core/models/bugs.py never re-declares it as a second, driftable list (A2.1/A2.10). `x-redact: false` marks the three fields (id, ts, reported_by) that write-time redaction must never scrub — every other string property is redacted by default. `status` has NO `picked` value (v0.5.0 FR2): the pick is the bundled definition commit, readable by pillar 2 (FR8 shape 5).

id.description: Stable identifier of this bug (kebab-case slug) — the record store's key.

ts.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp when the record was first appended (registration time).

reported_by.description: Agent or runtime that registered this record.

surface.description: Closed enum, one source (v0.5.0 FR2/A2.12): the 24 `dadaia_workspace/features/<name>/` packages on disk, plus the non-feature layers `core`/`infrastructure`/`cli`/`hooks`/`tests`/`public-assets`, plus the `unknown` sentinel for an unmappable legacy value. A contract test asserts the feature arm of this enum equals the on-disk package list; setup.cfg's `[importlinter:contract:features-no-cross-feature]` `modules =` list is completed to the same 24 by T-050-29 and is not yet the comparison target at this fold.

component.description: Free text: the `path#symbol` precision the fine-key analysis needs (component stays free text — only `surface` closed).

context.description: The active spec-context the bug was found in.

repro.description: The exact command / steps to reproduce.

status.description: Governance state. NO `picked` value (v0.5.0 FR2) — the pick is the bundled definition commit, not a status.

cause.description: The fix's own statement of what caused the bug — filled when resolved.

caused_by.description: The prior bug id this one was caused by, when this record is itself a reopen (a new id declaring `caused_by`).

lineage_source.description: How `caused_by` was established — e.g. `declared` (the fixer named it) or `text-reference` (inferred from prose, FR3 migration).

registration_commit.description: The 40-hex commit sha that first added this record's line, derived from git history (FR3) — never hand-written (D2).

registration_granularity.description: How precisely `registration_commit` identifies the adding commit.

resolved_commit.description: The 40-hex commit sha that fixed this bug, derived from git history (FR3) — null until an audit fills it (a commit cannot contain its own sha, AS-1).

resolution_granularity.description: How precisely `resolved_commit` identifies the fixing commit.

resolved_release.description: The release id that shipped the fix.

audited.description: The audit window id that reviewed this resolution — the one place `resolved_commit`/`resolution_granularity`/`audited` are ever written together, in a single atomic rewrite (FR14 pillar 1).

root_cause.description: Absent until the fix lands; immutable the moment it is written.

solution.description: Absent until the fix lands; immutable the moment it is written.

evidence_loop.description: The FR23 evidence triple, restored (v0.4.4, not re-invented): the red-loop command that reproduced the bug on the executed path, before any hypothesis.

evidence_seam.description: The FR23 evidence triple: the test file/node (the regression seam) that pins the fix.

evidence_diff.description: The FR23 evidence triple: the diff direction on the touched feature, prefixed 'net-negative:'/'net-positive:'/'net-neutral:' with a checkable rationale.

diff_direction.description: The closed-enum token `evidence_diff` already carries as free text — the fix-shape metric reads this field, not a parse of `evidence_diff` (FR14 metric 3).

superseded_by.description: The backlog/bug/release slug that supersedes this record — required when `status` is `superseded`; a sweep closure takes this status, never `resolved` (FR2).

migration_note.description: FR3 migration provenance note — e.g. an unmapped legacy `surface` counted as `unknown`, or a `caused_by` inferred from prose.
